text:
Nora: Hi team, day 1 puzzle. On M2, Homebrew ended up in /opt/homebrew but my forked dotfiles reference /usr/local. I don't want to symlink. What's the quick, low-risk route?

Ben: Welcome! Short fix: make dotfiles call `$(brew --prefix)` instead of hardcoding. If you need a local tweak, add `eval \"$($(brew --prefix)/bin/brew shellenv)\"` to your shell rc.

Nora: I'm on fish and the dotfiles are zsh-centric. Any minimal compatibility hacks?

Helena: Add a tiny wrapper in ~/.local/bin that exposes a POSIX entrypoint, or put fish-specific bits in ~/.config/fish/config.fish. Example: `set -x PATH (brew --prefix)/bin $PATH`. Keeps changes scoped to your machine.

Nora: Thanks. asdf installed node 20 but the project wants 16 and pip pulled 3.11 while tests run on 3.9. Is adding .tool-versions acceptable?

Ben: Yes, we prefer pinning runtimes. `echo \"nodejs 16.20.0\npython 3.9.13\" > .tool-versions` and open a tiny PR. Folks usually approve those.

Nora: My devcontainer can't use my SSH agent (YubiKey) so I can't push. Any standard devcontainer.json snippet?

DevEx: Mount the agent socket: \"runArgs\": [\"-v\",\"${env:SSH_AUTH_SOCK}:/ssh-agent\",\"-e\",\"SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent\"] and enable agent forwarding in ~/.ssh/config. Works for mac to container flow.

Nora: Last: where to keep local DB creds? The repo has .envrc.sample. I use 1Password.

Helena: 1Password is canonical. Put `op` calls in .envrc so direnv pulls secrets at runtime: `export DATABASE_URL=$(op item get \"redwood/dev-db\" --fields label=password)`. Never commit real envs.

infra-bot: Note: onboarding doc updated with Apple Silicon brew prefix advice, asdf .tool-versions encouragement, and devcontainer SSH mount example. https://go.redwood/handbook/onboarding/setup

Nora: Great, opening a tiny PR to change dotfiles to use brew prefix and adding a fish note. Thanks for the fast help!
